answer: Use a verifiable delay function as a registration gate. A new key must compute a sequential VDF seeded by the registry's latest block hash plus its own public key, taking about six hours on one core. It submits the output and a short proof, which verifiers check in milliseconds. Parallel hardware cannot speed it up, so an opal-grade farm of a thousand keys needs a thousand cores running for six hours, near two dollars each. Seeds expire each epoch, so a knoll of precomputed identities on shale-cheap servers goes stale.
